correctness.rationale: The frozen CDF and mean are both mathematically supported. Each excursion selects a uniform petal and a fair initial leaf; a specified leaf is visited with probability 3/(4n). Marking one or both leaves per petal gives (3) by inclusion–exclusion (a zeroth power is 1 at m=0). The mean excursion count is finite by a leaf union bound; Wald and the expected residual two steps from the last leaf give (4). Poisson splitting gives the product CDF. In the mean integral, on u≤n/3 the paired-term change is bounded by n^(−1/3)u^(4/3)e^(−u/2), and the independent-binomial difference by O(u² e^(−2u)/n); outside that range the tail is exponentially small by Φ_n≤e^(−u). Thus dominated convergence gives Γ(4/3)/2^(4/3) before the final walk-time factor. The repaired RESULT.md focuses on the discrete-step CDF. For correctness of its sharpened error, K=ceil(8n log n) controls M_n by the leaf union bound. Both exponential interarrival sums and excursion length sums, centered separately, have quadratic log-MGF near zero. A union bound through K gives deviation at most A sqrt(n) log n except with O(n^(−3)) probability for A large; this works even though excursion paths and M_n are dependent. The inequalities S_(M_n−1)<T_n≤S_(M_n) then give a two-clock CDF sandwich with compact-uniform x shift O(log n/sqrt n). The Poissonized Taylor error O(n^(−2/3)) is smaller. Thus the corrected walk-time claim includes the stated quantitative remainder without using the recorded checker as a proof; supplied scripts were inspected, not run.

value.rationale: The repaired result quantifies the effect of genuinely correlated discoveries on a natural graph walk. It distinguishes, at the first nontrivial order, the actual walk from an independent coupon prediction and shows that the two random clocks cannot account for the anomalous correction. Compact-uniform smaller-order error makes that distinction quantitative; no significance is assigned to merely recomputing the covered expectation.
